utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. May I remind of the affirmation that you made at the beginning of your evidence, which still applies. Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, good morning. We identified the problem with the binders yesterday, and it was you were missing the cover page of the Albanian version of what became Exhibit 498, former 65 ter 778.4, which is tab 4. So we make copies of the cover pages, if the usher can provide to the Judges and also to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And, also, Your Honours, we notice that this cover page had not been translated into English; and, yesterday, we translated and we uploaded but we will seek your permission to link the cover page, the English translation, to the already existing exhibit, 498.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And we can provide also the English translation of the cover page. It is also tab 4 of the binders. Finally, Your Honour, I would like to put in the record that, yesterday, in page 7431, line 20 and 7432, line 2, when we were working with the last document, the transcript read "Exhibit P416," when indeed we were working with, and I think I mentioned, Exhibit P460, 4-6-0.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Good morning, General.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please go to Exhibit P461, P461. It's in tab 3 of the binders.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, let me have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: We are waiting, General, to have the cover page in Albanian in e-court. Okay. We will work with the hard copy in Albanian. General, if we could go first to the cover page to the first page of this document. General we, again, see a document with a title, "Regulation on the Competencies and Work of the Brigade Command." Again, in the upper part of the document, we can read,"NLA, General Staff, Approved by NLA commander, Ali Ahmeti." We can see in the lower part of the document your name and "2001." General, did you produce this document?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: When did you produce it?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the period I mentioned. I worked from March, April, and early May. I can't specify the exact time, date, or week, but that was the period I worked.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. And, General, in order to produce this document, in which material, in which knowledge did you rely on?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to produce the regulation, the competencies, and the work of the brigade general provisions, and so on, there is such a rule in each and every army. In my case, I resorted to the army of Yugoslavia rules, the Albanian army, and other documents, because, as I already said, I had long experience in this field.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: To whom did you distribute these document, General, once it was produced?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We distributed it to the brigade commands.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could go to page 4 in e-court, which I think it will be page 3 for the hard copy. It's the Albanian page 3, my apology, also in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, in the second paragraph of this extract, which appears the title, "General Provision," we read: "The aim of this set of regulations is to define the duties, responsibilities, and rights of the officers and other staff members at the brigade command, so that they can carry out their functions and duties." General, which was the purpose of this regulation?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The aim of this regulation was to set the duties, responsibilities of all the persons involved in the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could go to page 2 of both of English and Albanian version, where we can see a table of contents.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, indeed, we can read in this table of contents different positions; for example, item 3, commander of the brigade; item 5, legal visor; item 6, head of the office for information and public relations; item 8, Chief of Staff; and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Also in the English version if we could go to the next page and keep the same in the Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: There are other positions like driver, worker, waiter. General, by the time that the Ohrid Agreement was signed, 13 August 2001, did the brigades -- had the brigades, all these positions filled?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not all of them, because the tendency was that, first, we completed the units that were engaged in fighting. So, beginning from the deputy commander squads, platoons, commanders of companies, and so on, only some important positions at the level of brigade were filled. So gradually we worked on filling all the other positions. I have to emphasise, however, that all these documents should be seen as documents that were needed and implemented gradually in conformity with the development and growth of the units of the National Liberation Army, because this army was not a formed army. It was an army in the process of formation abiding by such rules. So the filling of the positions in this army, based on these rules, was done according to the needs, assessments of the brigades, and the commanders of such brigades demanded the cadres they needed in various positions. So, as I said, there were brigade commanders first who were appointed, then their deputies, then the persons responsible for logistics; the key positions, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: You just mention that this army, the NLA, was an army in process of formation. What do you mean with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: By mean -- by means of this, I mean that the units of the NLA were formed of voluntaries [as interpreted] and became part of this army based on their abilities; and, normally, they were trained and given tasks to perform in the context of the units they were placed in.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: When you were producing this document, General, when did you expect that the conflict would end?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our wish was that it ended as soon as possible, but our aim was to reach a political understanding by the competent bodies in the Republic of Macedonia. But this is something we didn't know when it would be coming; therefore, our preparations were headed towards that direction. We expected the conflict to last very long.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And, General, would the level of implementation of these regulations be different, depending on the brigades? With that, General, I mean, if we focus on this regulation, the positions, would that be different, depending on the brigades?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The responsibility, on the level of brigade, the duties of a superior were the same, but the development of brigades varied; for example, when Brigade 113 was the first to be formed, then came Brigade 112, then 115, 116, 14. So none of them developed at the same time. They developed gradually, after they were completed with personnel and military equipment they needed. So the fulfilment of these tasks in theory were the same, but in practice that varied. It depended on the work done by each and every one of the personnel involved in that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: We will move on to another document. This is already an exhibit, Your Honours. Now we will move to 65 ter 778.8, which is tab 6 of the binder, and if we could go to the first page.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, we have in front of us the cover page of another document, which bears the title, "Regulations for the criteria involved in the classification of information of importance to the NLA, which must be kept a military or state secret and the methods entailed in the preservation thereof." Also, General, in the lower part of this document, on the right side, we see your name and the year, 2001. General, did you produce this document?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: When did you produce it, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the same time, during which I worked for the other documents, but after I finished the rules and formations.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, in order to produce this document, which sources did you rely on?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I relied exclusively on the rules of the Yugoslav army and state at that time, in Serbia, it was called; that is, a summary of laws and regulations on security in general."

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And once you finished producing this document, General, to whom did you distribute this document?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document, too, was distributed among the brigade commanders.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could go, please, to page 2 of both of English and the Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, if we focus on Article 1 just below item 1, General Rules, this Article reads, and I quote: "The set of regulations describes the criteria involved in the classification of important information for the NLA, which must be kept as a military or state secret and the means of protecting it in command structures, staff offices, units, and groupings of the Armed Forces, and in other organisations and associations which have access to such information." General, which was the purpose of this regulation?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose was to preserve the data and not make them public to people who are not competent of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could move to page 4 in both versions, I believe that in hard copies it will be page 3, and we focus in Article 15. In Albanian, in e-court, it should be the following page.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, Article 15 just below the item, Criteria for classifying secret information, Article 15 reads, and I quote: "The disclosure of document, arms and military equipment, measures, human resources, and other elements of importance to the NLA, by which the NLA and its preparations for the defence and safety of the country could, in some way, be jeopardised, constitute either military or state secrets, depending on their fields." And I end the quote. General, we just read here for the defence and safety of the country. Which country were you talking about? Which country did you mean?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, was among the goals of the NLA to establish a separate and independent country?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was shown in all our main communiques and main documents; namely, that the NLA was in favour of the full sovereignty and integrity of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could move, please, to the next page, it will be page 5 in e-court in both English and Albanian; and, for hard copy, it will be the page bearing number 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, you have in front of you Article 17, which defines a state secret, and I quote: "State secrets are such information about the NLA, information about the plans and preparatory defence activities of the NLA, in regard to which it has been determines that their disclosure might have negative repercussions for the defence and security of the country. "In particular, they are information relating to," and now in the document it is listed different examples; for instance, "item 2, Military plans of the NLA." General, if we move to Article 18 in the same page, I believe, the definition of military secret appears, and I quote: "A military secret constitutes information on the NLA, the plans, and preparatory activities of the NLA, vehicles, arms and military equipment, military facilities, important military formations, and all information impacting on the activities of the NLA. The publication or distribution thereof could have repercussions for the NLA and for the preparations for the defence of the country." General, in a nutshell, which would be the main difference between a state secret and a military secret, in simple terms?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To put it simply, for us, a state secret consisted of war plans, formations, and duties, including also our assessment of them; whereas, part of military secrets are equipment, better security of our positions, even though they were open to the army and the police of Macedonia. They were known to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this stage, I would seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P500, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, you mention in your statement that the origins of the NLA, in paragraph 16 of your statement, you mention that could be found in the dissatisfaction of the Albanian population as they were being excluded from the public life, from the public institutions. You also mention that the NLA explained its political goals in communique number 6, which was reproduced almost entirely in the Ohrid Agreement. That's in paragraph 31 of your statement, General. Could you briefly explain which was the content of this communique, meaning the main goals of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Through this communique, the NLA General Staff insisted on making known its aims embodied in the NLA. From what I recall, this statement, or communique, had, as its first point, the commitment of the NLA to preservation of the territorial integrity of the Republic of Macedonia; then, the need for impartial international intervention to resolve the conflict; then, the census of the population to be taken in the Republic of Macedonia; then, amendment of the constitution of the Republic of Macedonia. To put it in simpler terms, we demanded that the amendment the preamble to the constitution of the Republic of Macedonia for Albanians to be a state constituent element in the Republic of Macedonia. In that point, it is written that Macedonia should be an Albanian-Macedonian or Macedonian-Albanian state, depending on the formulation. We believe that by carrying out such amendments to the constitution and its preamble, we would be free of discrimination in the field of culture, science, education, state institutions, and so on. Further on, in this communique, we demanded that the neighbouring states not side with any of the parties but contribute to the conclusion of this process; and, finally, we appeal to the Macedonian mothers not to let their children become prey to the state officials in Macedonia at the time. This is more or less, in summary, the content of communique number 6.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Can you recall when this communique was issued, approximately?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I remember. This communique was issued on the 9th of March, and it was published in the Albanian-speaking media and maybe also some Macedonian-speaking medium. It was broadcast by such information media. We believe that both international and home public were informed of the aims of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you reproduce these goals of the NLA in another significant document, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These goals were our permanent demand; therefore, they were included also in other documents. Almost the same content, but rather better regulated, is expressed also in the memorandum that the political representative of the NLA, Mr. Ali Ahmeti, addressed to the United Nations, its honourable chairman, the Secretary-General of NATO, the chairman of the European Commission, the OSCE president, and the entire public at home and abroad.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And, General, again, if you can recall approximately when this memorandums with sent to these international institutions?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The end of April, maybe on the 24th of April, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Of 2001, correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. We are talking all the time of 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could please move to Exhibit P486, which is tab 10 of the binders, Your Honours, and if we could go to the first page, which is the cover page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, we have in front of us a cover page of a document which, again, reads, "NLA, General Staff, Approved by NLA commander, Ali Ahmeti," and bears the title, "Development of moblisation and personnel and material formation of the General Staff." We can read, actually, in the lower part, again, your name, General. Did you produce, General, this document?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: When did you produce it, approximately?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the same framework, when I worked on the formation. In general, I worked on these documents during March, April, and part of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, again, in order to produce this document, which sources did you rely on? Which knowledge did you use?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since 1969, I was Chief of Staff; first, at a municipal level, which compared to a brigade in army terms; then, during the Kosovo war, I was Chief of Staff of the Dukagjini zone; and then I was Chief of Staff of the KPC. So I did not lack the knowledge to draft and to create a General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And, General, again, to whom did you distribute this document once it was produced?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document remained in the General Staff with me. The commander, of course, had it as well. And, based on this document, I insisted that the posts be filled in gradually.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could move to page 2 of this document, which is page 1 in the -- in the hard copy. It's the first chart.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, we see here a chart which has the heading basic mobilisation plan. This chart contains different columns. The first column bears the title, "Organs." General, is "organs" a correct translation from Albanian?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Albanian, it's the "organigram."

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Excuse me, my mistake. It reads, "Unit." So I want to ask you General, whether "unit" -- because in English, we have the translation "unit." Was "unit" the correct translation from the Albanian.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, where it writes "staff," perhaps a mistake has been made. Maybe it should be stated as "organ," "department." Similarly, to other formations and development charts, maybe this "unit" was transferred to this chart automatically, but otherwise it should be "the organ."

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And we are talking about the first column, right?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where it is written "the unit."

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: In this chart, we can read, in the next columns: "Number and name of unit," or organs, "place of basic mobilisation plan." We read: "General, high ranking officer, officer," some other positions, then "uniforms and weapons." General, which was the purpose of these regulation of this chart?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we are talking in terms of the development of mobilisation, the aim of this chart was in order to have a clear picture as per every organ, in order to show the number of participants and their equipment. While in development, these were worked on, on individual terms, for every formation individually.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could --

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: So, here, we have a collective information and duties of the respective organs.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, if we could move to the next page, both English and Albanian. Do you see, General, your position in this column, in the first column?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, The Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: According to the chart, General, you are marked below the category "General," and you were given a uniform and a handgun. Is this information accurate?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct. I had a uniform and a handgun.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document is already an exhibit, 486, so I won't seek to tender it. Now I will move to 65 ter 778.13, which is tab 8 of your binders, and if we could go to the first page. To the next one, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, we have in front of us a chart which bears the heading, "Soldier's personal and collective weaponry card." Well, first of all, General, which was the purpose of this chart?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I can see here, we have a -- an armed squad that received or were issued weapons, and each of its members signed for the weapons that they were issued with.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Indeed, we have a first column with names listed. Second column, for example, reads: "Kalashnikov, weapon number." If we go a bit to the right, we see: "Ballots," and also "the weapon number, grenades, sniper rifle." And then at the end, the last column requires the signature of the person. General, did you produce this chart, this particular chart?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This chart was produced by the base units, by the brigade, or at a level of the battalion or the company. While here, what we see before us, it's a chart about a squad and the weapons that members of this squad were issued with.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: So at which level these charts would be kept, would be filled, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Such a form would be filled in at a company level, which is divided into platoons and squads, while the records were kept at a level of battalions and brigades.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And whom within these units, General, will be in charge with filling this information?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person directly involved with this issue in the company, and these records should be at the possession of the squad commander, so that he is familiar with the weapons that are issued to his squad.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And when you say "the person directly involved with this issue in the company," which person do you mean? Which position do you refer to?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person in charge; that is, the company commander and the person that he assigns with the duty of keeping these records; then these forms go to the battalion, to the brigade. I'm talking in terms of serious and completed army. So as I described it earlier, this was in period of formation, and I wish you to understand me within those terms.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P501, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could move to 65 ter 778.14, which is tab 9. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, again, we have here another chart with the heading, "Soldier's personal card of clothing and other personal equipment." Which is the purpose of this chart, General?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do we have some problems with the translation?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, did you hear my question? Which is the purpose of this chart?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose of this chart is to have a well-kept record regarding the equipment of the officers of the NLA, who were issued weapons and who signed for these weapons and are responsible for them.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Well, General, in particular, the chart that we have in front of us deals with clothing. If you can look, General, to the chart, you can see in the first column, the names; then, the second column, for example, trousers; then jackets, T-shirts, shoes, flakjackets; and at the end, we see the signature of the person who was issued this material, General. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Which was then the purpose of this chart, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose of this chart was to create a clear picture of the clothing that was issued to members of the units of and brigades and the persons that were issued. And based on these charts, then the need for filling in the shortcomings would be clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you develop these charts, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These charts were made at a level of brigade logistics department.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will seek to tendered this chart into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P502, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could move to Exhibit P487, which is tab 14. Your Honours, this -- if we could go to the first page of the Albanian version, which is the one that shows the map in the e-court. Your Honour, we can provide to yourself and the colleagues a bigger map; also to the witness, and one for the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, we have in front of us a map which bears the title, "Directive of military operation." On the upper right side, we see the date, 13 of June, 2001; and in the lower part of the document, we see the stamp and the signature of Ali Ahmeti. General, who produced this map?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked in the production of this directive.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you work, did you produce it on the 13th of June, 2001, as the document reads?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I want to clarify something, if permitted. This document is titled, "Freedom 2." On the right-hand side, where the word "secret" is mentioned and the date, the first part is in fact, "Freedom 1." And on the map, it is marked with yellow, and it starts from the north at the village of Slupcane and continues along. Do you want me to continue explaining this?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, General. If you allow me, I will keep asking the questions, and then we can go on slowly so Their Honours can understand. General, first --

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. Why did you produce this map? Which was the main purpose of this document, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In an army, the military plans are conducted on maps and are explained in writing. I worked on this map for planning purposes and for explaining to the commander a military operation plan.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General. And just to clarify, did you produce this document on the date which is indicated in the upper right side, 13 of June, 2001?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 13th of June.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Now, General, we are going to look at the different parts of this map. First of all, General, if you could explain, what were you indicating with the areas which are depicted in yellow?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I tried to explain it earlier. I interfered, I guess, with your question. This document is titled, "Liria" or "Freedom 2." The previous document was titled, "Freedom 1." Only that part of the document marked with yellow was prepared. So, at the time, it was necessary to realise that part in order to pass into this new plan, because the Liberation Army at that time had been only on those positions. Then, with the second map, with the green, it's marked what should be done next.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: So the parts -- the territories which are indicated in yellow, which are showing, General, exactly? Just focus on the yellow parts, General.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The yellow parts indicate the location or the area where the NLA had established its authority, where it had its positions, excluding the Kercove part and the city of Diber - and I'm specifying here the city of Diber because there were some positions north of Diber - and with the exclusion of Struga, while positions were present at all other locations which are marked with yellow here.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: These three locations, these three positions that you just mentioned, Kercove, Diber, and Struga, are indicated in yellow, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because the volunteers were ready, but we did not issue any order for them to be sent there and become operative.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Can you explain us where are these areas. Do you see them indicated, marked in the map, the yellow?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mali i Zi i Shkupit, Skopska Crna Gora, so from the border with neighbouring country on the north, above Aracinovo at Mojance village; then in the area of Radush, the Sar Mountain; and on the entire left side of Tetova, in the municipality of Mavrov; in the area of villages of Tanuse and some others, which I cannot read at the moment, and Kercove.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I don't mean to interrupt you. I want to know is whether these areas, these territories that you mentioned, are indicated already in the yellow on the map. Either in the main yellow part or in the isolated circles that we see, are they depicted in yellow?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They are depicted in yellow, with the exception of the places that I mentioned: Diber, Kercove, and Struga.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: So these are not indicated in yellow. They are not marked with yellow, these three locations?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are marked with yellow, because as I said, the volunteers were at the state of readiness and waiting for or order, but we did not issue an order and they did not become operative.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Maybe if we can take the pen and the General can indicate.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, you will be given an electronic pen, and I will ask to you look at the screen and to indicate where these three locations you mentioned, Kercove, Struga, and Diber, are . Let's start with Kercove, which area?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, just one second, General. The gentleman will help you out.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you could move it up a little bit, in order to see Kercove.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you see Kercove in this map, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: A little bit, if you could just enlarge it. This is the part here.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay, General, I would like, please, yeah, indicate where Kercove, is, where it's located.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: So you were referring to this area. Could you write number 1, please, General, next to this circle.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. Now do you see in the same map Struga?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Can you write number 2.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: For the record, the General has indicated that Struga is the circle in the lower left side; and circle, indicated with number 1, is the yellow circle more in the centre of the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And the third location, General, I believe that you mentioned Diber. Where is it located? Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Can you write number 3, please?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: The General has indicated a circle, which is more on the left of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, we see also more, if we look north, another area which is depicted in a yellow circle, which is separated from the main yellow area. Which territory were you indicating there?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is an area where the units were supposed to take positions later on. There are two green arrows showing which ones should go there, but I cannot read it on the map at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, I'm talking about a yellow circle more in the north, just below and on to the right of the main yellow area, which is isolated, separated from the main yellow area. Do you see that, at least in the hard copy, General? I think it is written in the centre, "1/201," but I may be wrong.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are many elements here that are the integral part of the war, but I don't know which one you're referring to at the moment. Specifically, which one? Which unit?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I'm referring to a circle in yellow which is separated from the main territory, from the many yellow area, which is to the right of the map. But if you are not able to see, General, I will move on. It's a bit -- it's to the left of Skopje. I believe that is below Tetovo.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Below Tetovo?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It cannot be on the left of Skopje and below Tetovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: My apologies. Maybe I'm not well familiar with the geography.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps if you looked between Skopje and Tetovo, just to the south of a line joining those two, and nearer to Tetovo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see it. It is a mark for a company that should be formed from the brigade, 112th --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The interpreter is not sure about the number.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Brigade of Tetovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you repeat the number of the brigade, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: 112th, Mujdin Aliu Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please draw a circle on the screen indicating this area, General.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I understand it, it is about this unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understood it correctly.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, General.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And I thank you, Your Honour, for the help.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If you could please write number 4.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Maybe, at this point, I will tender this document, because we may lose the markings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honours. I apologise for interfering in the examination of my colleague, but the Defence is not clear, and I think it would be good for the transcript also to clarify the circles marked with 1, 2, and 3. I think that it remained unclear whether inside the circles were the areas that were not under the control of the NLA, which were not under the NLA control. Then the question would be about the number 4, whether the number 4 marks an area that was not under the NLA control. At least this is how I understood it, so if my colleague can clarify it and the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I'm happy to clarify it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, could you explain to us whether the areas that you marked with number 1, 2, 3, and 4 were at the moment that you were preparing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think they're different, so perhaps you better separate the fourth from 1, 2, and 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, could you explain to us whether the areas, which you have marked with number 1, 2 and 3, were under the NLA control by the date that you produced this map, meaning 13 of June, 2001.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were people in combat readiness who, upon taking orders, would fight.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: What about the area indicated with number 4? Was the NLA deployed in that region as well?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But it was the duty of Brigade 115 to develop, in case this operation would be performed, to operate in that area with part of its units.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Maybe I'm a bit confused, General, but I believe that you mentioned 112th Brigade before. I'm talking about the region indicated with number 4.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Brigade 112 should operate, come to the assistance of 115, in case it needed it, because the aim of this operation was to close Skopje-Tetovo road. Only in that case would this unit go there.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: So to have to clear, in the area depicted number 4, what -- was NLA presence, or it was a forthcoming action, to be undertaken?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The text, the written text is attached to the map, and the text clearly states the purpose of the operation. On the 13th of June, work was under way to expand the units of the NLA, but the deployed -- there were not specifically deployed units there.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: At this stage, Your Honour, I'll tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can I just be a little more clear, Mr. Ostreni. Do I correctly understand, in respect of the areas marked 1, 2, and 3, that you had, you say, members of the NLA in position in a state of combat readiness, but they had not been given orders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were staying in their own respective homes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So they had not been mobilised.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, they were not. They kept in touch only with their leaders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. And in the area marked 4, there were not people in position, but orders had been given to the 112th Brigade to be supported, if necessary, by the 115th Brigade, to gain control of that area, with a view to blocking the Tetovo-Skopje road. Is that what you were saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With a minor difference; namely, that 112th would support Brigade 115, because brigade 115 was closer to Skopje, so it could do that; whereas, the other brigade would go as reinforcement on the right side of the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. This will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P503, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, we also see some areas indicated in green. Were these territories occupied by the NLA, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't use the term "occupied," Your Honour, because that is our country. We cannot occupy it. Secondly, the colour green shows the direction that the operation of the NLA would take to realise the operation, military operation, which should be developed in the future.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And now if we could please go to the plan, to the document, which is page 1 in the English version and page 2 in the Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, just to follow up in your answer, you mention that the colour green shows the direction that the operation of the NLA would take to realise the whole operation, the military operation, in the future. Was this operation, which should be undertaken in the green areas, ever implemented, ever performed by the NLA?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As an operation per se, it was not implemented.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we please could about to the document itself, which is page 1, as I mentioned, in the English, page 2 in the Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, we will look at the document closely in a minute. But before that, did you produce this document?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. And on the left side, you see Gzim Ostreni on the lower left side.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: In the lower part, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, it will be in the last page of the English document.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And, General, did you produce it at the same time as the map?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: That would be June --

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two documents that go together. First, you draw up the idea in writing, then you put it in the map; then, again, you first expound it in writing, providing for every details.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. General, that would be June 2001, right?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And which was the purpose of this document, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose of this document was to coordinate the actions of the brigades of the NLA and to help plan the realisation of a military operation. The reason for preparing it was that the NLA, at that time, was in a position, because it had reached a considerable number of personnel, to pass on to a joint operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And, General, if we focus in the first paragraph, just below the title, the heading, "3, Ideas for conducting the operation," and I will quote: "While continuing to increase of the number of units in the brigades, in line with the establishment, active combat operations will be undertaken with a view to breaking up and eliminating the enemy's troops, so as to block and take over the towns and main roads of western Macedonia as rapidly as possible." General, which is the significance of this particular paragraph?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this paragraph is clear. The brigades should push further the forces of the army and the police, and take up other positions which are marked here, and you can see them also in the map; that is, to carry out a complete movement in the direction of the east.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And these positions, these will be the ones indicated with green colour in the map, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. They are marked in green.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we keep in the English version, page 1, General, a little bit below to the main paragraph, we can read: "The operation will be conducted in two stages: In stage one by 10 July," and just below, "in stage 2, by the end of July." You describe several operations. Were these operations ever implemented, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were never implemented.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could go to page 2, please, of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, just we see here a heading with a the title,"4, Deployment and tasks of UCK forces." You are describing different operations with regards to different brigades. If we focus on the first paragraph, General, when you are talking about the 113th Brigade, we can reed that: "The 113th Brigade will, by 10 of July, make preparations to capture and cut off the town of Kumanovo," and also you mentioned the blocking of two nearby roads. General, did the NLA ever succeed in capturing Kumanovo?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Which was the significance of this operation, General, for the NLA?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You cannot leave a war in the middle, unless the Ohrid Agreement was signed. Unless the politicians didn't come to terms among themselves, then the army and the police would continue with their fighting. The NLA, also, had its own plan of operations to bring pressure, greater pressure, to bear upon them in order to have its demands, its purposes and goals expressed in communique number 6 in the memorandum, realised.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And, General, if we move to the second paragraph, where it is mentioned: "At the same time, the 113th Brigade troops holding the village of Aracinovo will form the 1st Battalion of the 114th Brigade and gradually continue recruiting to full strength at brigade level." I'll just stop there, General. Was the 114th Brigade ever formed?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Brigade 114 was formed, as far as I can remember, on the 1st of July, and it had to break away from Brigade 113 because of the great number of soldiers in Brigade 113, which gave rise to the establishment of the other brigade which was planned to be form.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, if we move now to the third paragraph, when you are talking about the 115th Brigade, I quote: "The 115th Brigade battalion, in the Derventa area, will continue efforts to expand at brigade level, forming a 2nd Battalion." General, was this battalion ever created within the 115th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 2nd Battalion was not created as a separate battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Now, in the same paragraph, General, you mention that also the 115th Brigade will make preparations to take some areas, in accordance to an order. General, did the 115th Brigade ever took -- ever take over these additional territories?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It should be done on special orders by the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And was this order of issued, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we move a bit below, General, we can also read here that: "The 115th Brigade will assist the 112th Brigade in breaking up and eliminating the forces located in Polog, as well as in closing the Skopje-Velse road. Were these operations ever carried out, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat your question? Which brigade are you asking me? I'm not clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, General. I'm just reading from the document. In the paragraph which relates to the 115th Brigade, it reads like -- I believe it will be the third line, starting from the end of this paragraph: "The 115 Brigade will assist the 112th Brigade in breaking up and eliminating," excuse me, "the forces located in Polog, as well as enclosing the Skopje-Velse road." I was asking whether these operations were ever carried out, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not carried out on any orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Now we move to another paragraph, which deals with the 112 Brigade in the area of Tetovo, and here we can read that: "The 112 Brigade will send a company to close the Skopje-Tetovo road." General, this road was, indeed, cut off in the beginning of August. Which was the importance of this operation of this action?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Simply, Your Honour, we believe that the facts stated my colleague in her question should perhaps be established first.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, was the road which -- which communicates as Skopje and Tetovo ever cut off by the NLA?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not cut off on any orders by the General Staff. It was cut off, as I heard later, by an operation undertaken by the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Which was the significance, the importance, of this action in military terms, General, for the NLA, the cutting off of this road?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we talk about the duties of Brigade 112, that is a very important one, because that would cut off the communication of the forces of the army and the police which were deployed in Polog and the other forces that were in Skopje. It would make impossible bringing in of reinforcements of reservist forces. That would be done in cooperation with 116 Brigade, which had to come at the cross-roads from Kercove, which goes to Tetovo. Polog would be cut off on both sides. The forces that would remain there would have to fight. The forces of the army and the police would have to fight with -- sorry, we'd have to face many problems and challenges.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, in order to speed up a little bit, in this document, also some instructions -- some operations are foreseen with regards to the 116th Brigade, with regards to the 111th Brigade. Were these operations ever carried out?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could move, please, to page 3 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, we see in item 5, "Balance of forces," and I will quote the paragraph: "The balance of forces on the western Macedonia front is currently a 1:5 ratio, in favour of the government troops, and they are greatly superior in terms of equipment. By the end of July, it will still be 1:2. And in the field of equipment, it will remain the same." General by the end of July, did you reach the [indiscernible] ratio, the ratio that you mention in this paragraph, 1:2?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As is known, the cease-fire started to take effect on the 6th of July. So we stopped our efforts to reinforce the NLA because we had great hopes in the forthcoming agreement to be carried out with the mediation of international forces. Voluntaries [as interpreted] did come, but we, as I said, kind of suspended the work because the expense of the number was linked with the greater logistical support and equipment. But we were very much hoping that this fight taking place between our forces and the forces of the government would come to an end and we would reach an agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, did you ever reach this ratio, 1: 2? It's a "yes" or "no" answer, General.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that the NLA reached the number 5.000 troops at the time we were preparing the operations. The overall number of the forces of army were stated to be about 20.000 at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And, General --

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that that was a realistic -- the realistic assessment of the ratio would be 1:4 or 1:5. In my view, at the time, the number of forces directly engaged in the front line, without counting those who were working in the logistics, in the administration, in the medical staff and so on, the proportion came to be 1:5.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, you mentioned that the operations, which were foreseen by the brigades that you indicate in this plan, were not carried out. You just mentioned that before. Why these operations were never implemented?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because they were planned as of 10th of July, while the cease-fire was in force on the 6th of July, it was signed at midnight of 5th of July. So we were in a state of readiness and also awaiting a peaceful solution to the situation in Macedonia. So it was our wish for this conflict to end with dialogue and negotiations.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have two more questions with regards to this document. I don't know if you want me to finish it..

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, in the same paragraph that we are looking at, we can read that: "The morale of the UCK forces plays a significant role in ameliorating the balance of forces between the government forces of the UCK, and will alter the ratio to a proportion 1:10, in favour of the UCK infantry." General, which is the significance of this factor of the morale, the high morale among the NLA?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The experience of the apprising army shows that their members are volunteers. They are not forced to take up weapons, but they do take up arms voluntarily, by their free will. So all recent wars in the territory of former Yugoslavia in the Balkans shows that the ratio between the volunteers and mobilised soldiers is uncomparable. For a soldier, it is a shame to go back home. We had cases when the volunteers, the wounded tried to go back on the front line. So I don't want someone to be misunderstood, but the mobilised soldiers cannot be compared in any way to the volunteer.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we focus on the last two lines ...

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And for that we have to move to the last page in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: ... the last two of this document reads: "International conventions must be strictly respected during all operations by UCK troops, and the treatment of civilians and facilities must be at the required level." General, which is the significance of this sentence?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sentence is of utmost importance. It prevails in many of our documents. The National Liberation Army protected the civilians, looked after them, and at all times feared the failure to control or to instigate -- otherwise instigate a civil war. So chapter 3, item 5 precisely defines how an officer in his morale should be clear in that issues, to treat all the citizens of Macedonia equally without making any difference as per their religion or ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Just to finish up, General, when you mentioned chapter 3, item 5, which document are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Rules of Service of the NLA, which deals with the morale of the members of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will take the first break now, resume at five past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Could we please go to 65 ter 676. It's tab 15 of the binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, you mentioned in paragraph 31 of your statement that the NLA General Staff communicated with the public through communiques. I will show now you a list of communiques. General, we have if front of us a communique signed with a the name of Ali Ahmeti in the lower part, and it starts in item 1 reading: "On the 3rd of May 2001, they launched an attack offensive fences without sparing even civilians in the Lipkovo Kumanovo defence area of the 113th Brigade." Then two lines below, it follows: "During the fighting, the UCK NLA removed five killed and 11 wounded from their ranks; while on the UCK sided, there were neither dead nor wounded." General, are you familiar with the context in which this communique was drafted and issued.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This communique was issued in conditions of preparations for the operation MX-2 of the forces of the army and the police. During this time, the shelling continued, the shelling of the territory; and in one word, there was fierce fighting on those positions between the NLA and the ARM.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, are you aware of the date, of the approximate date when this communique was issued?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember the date, but I have it before me so it should be after the 3rd of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. General, if we keep reading in item 2, it mentions that two civilians were killed by the shelling of the villages. Item 3 reads: "We appeal to the government and the president to halt the violence against the civilian population and to stop further destruction of our shared country while commencing talks to resolve the problems." Item 4 reads: "Only a halt to the conflict and the commencement of constructive dialogue will serve the cause of peace and stability in the Balkans and the building of a democratic society, where we will all live happily." General, we see, in item 4, that the NLA is asking is for dialogue, in order to achieve peace and stability. With whom did you want to engage in such a dialogue, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the government, starting from the president of the country, the prime minister, so with the government of the Republic of Macedonia, and, of course, with the ruling political parties. But if you talk to the government, it means that you have, in fact, talked with the representatives of the political parties.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And, General, why it was important to engage in a dialogue with the political parties, with the government? Why it was important for the NLA?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was important because it was necessary to bring the war to the end by having our goals for the rights of the Albanians in the Republic of Macedonia achieved, and this could be performed only by further democraticisation of our country.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did the Macedonian authorities ever respond to your demand for dialogue, at that time, beginning May 2001?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, they didn't. Instead, they continued with the operation MX-2, on the 8th of May. I'm not maybe precise on the day, but it should be during this period.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General. Now, if we look at item 5 of this document, of the communique, we can read, and I quote: "We appeal to the international community to use its authority to bring an end to the war and contribute to peace-building in Macedonia." Why the NLA was requesting the intervention of the international community, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because there was a misunderstanding between the Albanians and the government, or the other the side that they represented, the Macedonian people, regarding our rights. As it is stated in part of the memorandum, we were led by the example of Switzerland, Belgium, and other western European countries, that based on a dialogue, you with reach cohabitation. We were convinced that we, Albanians, alone, without the mediation of the international community, will not achieve our goals. We could not reach any dialogue with the competent organs of the government.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And which was the reaction of the international community to your request at the time? I'm talking about the beginning of May 2001, General.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During this time, it was our impression that the international community had information that the Republic of Macedonia is a country of peace, that the Albanians and other minorities enjoyed their rights; and in this sense, of course, they supported the government of the Republic of Macedonia in the beginning, in their actions. But this standpoint began to change gradually.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, general.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek it tendered this communique.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P504, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please go to 65 ter 675. It's tab 16 of the binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, again, we see another communique, but this time the producer it reads, in the lower part of the document, "General Staff." I'm going to read to you the first paragraph: "Fighting between Macedonian government military and police forces and the 100th Brigade in the municipalities of Kumanovo and Lipkovo continued with undiminished intensity on 4th May. The Macedonian police and army have been bombing and shelling from surface and air. "The targets of the destructive artillery projectiles attacks were not only the positions occupied by the heroic and invincible soldiers of the UCK, but also the houses and places of refuge of the Albanian civilian population." General, are you aware in which context this communique was issued?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a day following the communication we discussed earlier. As I said earlier, this is in line of the operation that was to continue. I think that the territory was being surveilled at that time, and the positions as well. So there was regular exchange of fire between members of the NLA and the forces of the army and the police, but with a small distinction; that is, that the forces of the army and the police were applying artillery weaponry, helicopters, and the devastation of a greater scale because of the strength of the weapons that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Indeed, General. I believe it is the third paragraph, at least in English version, which mentions -- actually, lists the Macedonian weapons used in the attack: Military Mi-24 helicopters, 115-millimetre Howitzers, 122-millimetre calibre cannons and mortars, et cetera. In the next paragraph of the communique, General, it is mentioned 20 casualties. There were 20 casualties among the Macedonian forces, and three of them were kept as prisoners. If we read below, in the last four lines, it says: "The Albanian civilians were also casualties in this attack. Seven were killed and many others wounded." And, finally: "The military and police attacks continued today, 5 May, but the NLA remains unflinching in their positions." General, are you aware who issued this communique?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This communique was issued by the General Staff based on a report it received from 113th Brigade, Izmet Jashari Kumanova Brigade, in Kumanovo municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will seek to tendered this communique.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P505, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please go to 65 ter 677, which is tab 17.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, we have a communique dated 6th of May, 2001, and also produced by Ali Ahmeti. It reads in the first paragraph, and I quote: "The General Staff of the NLA is monitoring with deep concern the decisions of the state organs, which have demonstrated that the conflict is one of major dimensions; and, as a consequence, whole populated areas have been destroyed and many civilians, including children, have been killed.." General, which decisions taken by the state organs indicate that the conflict was, indeed, a conflict of major dimensions, if you are aware?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Macedonian parliament, on the 15th -- or rather, 16th, 17th, and 18th of March, held a session on the security situation in the Republic of Macedonia, and reached the conclusions, pursuant to which the Ministry of Defence and of the Interior was to carry out its duties in order to establish -- re-establish peace in the Republic of Macedonia. If you read carefully these conclusions at the time, we understood them in the following way: They brought a decision that peace and stability can be brought back only if the National Liberation Army is destroyed. That's why we thought, at the time, that the Ministry of Defence and the General Staff of the army of the Republic of Macedonia, the president, and everybody were engaged in this direction. The operations continued against the National Liberation Army. I would like to mention in this context that during this phase, there wasn't a position by the parliament to proclaim a phase of war in the Republic of Macedonia; while in reality, all their forces were being used in combat. The Macedonian government, in the beginning of April, brought a decision to expand the border belt, which, in ordinary conditions, was 100 to 300 metres. It expanded to ten kilometres in the western part of the territory, in order to enable the engagement of the army and the police in this depth of territory.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General. Now if we go whack to the communique, just after the line that I just read, we can read: "Rapid action is needed to prevent this catastrophic situations, so that the problems that are presented for resolution are to the benefit of both our peoples, to turn a new page of history, so that we may have live together in a democracy and for progress, which is the immediate goal of all civilised people." General, just briefly, what is the significance of this sentence that I just read out to you?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The significance of this sentence, as we deem it, is very high. Our goal was not to divide ourselves as Albanians from of Macedonians. Our aim was not to divide the Republic of Macedonia. So this abyss that could be created by bloodshed would have turned into an obstacle for further co-existence. That's why we aimed at negotiations because we wanted to live together with the Macedonians. Once the war ended, we wanted to be close with our co-citizens, with our friends, and with our neighbouring countries.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: In the next paragraph, General, it is, indeed, mentioned that: "The UCK is striving to use force in a mature fashion and in self-defence, with the aim of creating the most suitable arena possible for a general dialogue." General, the word "dialogue" is mentioned here again. During the conflict, was the NLA always open to dialogue with the Macedonian authorities?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The NLA was always open to dialogue and opted for dialogue. It pleaded for the war to be brought to an end as soon as possible, so that this division between Albanians and Macedonians become insignificant and not have any impact in the future.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General. If we move five lines below, the communique goes on, indicating, and I quote: "We have expressed, and continue to express, a readiness and willingness to announce a cease-fire, so long as you, Mr. Trajkovski and Mr. Georgievski, do the same; as only thus can we save our common fatherland from destruction, only thus can we alleviate the affliction of our mothers and our families." General, we just read that the NLA was willing and ready to announce a cease-fire. Why were they -- was the NLA willing to reach a cease-fire?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: A cease-fire is always a condition for talks, so we always showed a goodwill and great wish to put an end to the war, to sit at the negotiating table. This was not an adventure. It was a dangerous war, dangerous for all citizens. There was also a danger for it to become a civil war. That's why we were always ready to sit and negotiate. If you follow the history of all developments up to the signing of the agreement, you won't find any instance that would demonstrate that the NLA was against negotiations, be they with international community, with NATO and other representatives of the international community, or the local government authorities.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Which was the response of the Macedonian -- from the Macedonian side to your request at that time? We're talking about 6th of May, 2001.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was issued on the 6th of May; and, to my recollection, the offensive MX-2 began in these villages. So their response was to undertake offensive, the response of the forces of the army and the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this communique.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P506, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we move to 65 ter 727, which is tab 18.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, we have here a communique dated 8th of May, 2001, and also issue by Ali Ahmeti. It reads: "Bearing in mind the need to inform national and international public opinion that the NLA has met conditions for its legalisations, we hereby declare." Item 1 mentions that: "The NLA functions as a disciplined military organisation." Item 2 mentions that: "The NLA has its own uniforms, ranks, and insignia." General, I will stop there for a second. Why was this communique issued at that time?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you see the date here, it's 8th of May, 2001, it is a time when majority of documents that we reviewed here were already prepared and were being distributed to the brigades at this time, in order for them to start reorganisation and implement these documents. So it was necessary to make this communique public for the internal and external public opinion; to familiarise them with the NLA functioned, its hierarchy; and to make them aware that the competent institutions that wish to talk with representatives of the NLA, they can to so by talking about its commander. In other words, this was to make public that the NLA was becoming to be institutionalised.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General. Item 3 of this communique reads, and I quote: "The method of organisation of the UCK, as well as living and working conditions within the UCK in line with current regulations, ensure that the UCK conducts its operations in accordance with the stipulations of international law, fully respected by all members, especially by the General Staff." Item 4 mentions that: "The General Staff and the entire UCK respect, and will always respect, the Geneva Convention during their operations." Finally, item 5 indicates that: "The General Staff will undertake all necessary measures for cooperation with The Hague Tribunal, as being the legitimate organ in this respect against all those who abuse their function within the UCK, and whose conduct violates the rules in force within the UCK, and also valid laws and war crimes in particular." General, here we have read international law, Geneva Convention, and valid laws and war crimes. What is the significance of this -- of this mentions, General, of the respect of international or Geneva Convention and war crimes law?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The significance of what you read is to make aware all the subordinates in the brigades of the General Staff of the NLA, that all those who will violate rules and laws will be held responsible for their acts and will be brought to justice during war, if possible, or after war. So that's why it was necessary to underline that the life of the civilians, of women, children, elderly, and all other non-combatants, be safeguarded; and, of course, the prisoners of war as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will seek to tendered this communique.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something else as well, regarding this communique?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: But just briefly, General, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will be very brief, very brief. We knew that there was The Hague Tribunal in place. This was so not only to make us more aware of our duty to realise our duties, but also to remind all the members not to commit any criminal offences. So it was with seriousness that we, the formations of the army, respected all the rules and the orders of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General. Your Honours, I will seek to tender this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P507, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please go to 65 ter 678. It's tab 19.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, we have, in front of us, a communique dated the 10th of May, 2001. And if we move to the second page of the English original, we see your name at the end of this document. General, did you issue this communique? Did you produce this communique?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, but you have to look at the date, whether this was issued on this day. It is my communique issued after the operation undertaken by the army and the police in Tetovo on the 25th of March.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And we will go now --

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whereas, the communique was written after the operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General. We will go now to the text of the communique. But why, at the time, did you feel the need to produce this communique?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
