utterances.text: It was necessary, in my opinion, because without a decision by parliament, the Republic of Macedonia, its competent bodies, were using the army to resolve internal issues, which, at that time, ran counter to the constitution of Macedonia. By means of this communique, I wanted to inform each and everyone at home and abroad that force is being against the Albanians, unlawful forces are being used or -- a lawful force of the forces is being used.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: What do you mean by that the forces were being used counter against what the constitution of Macedonia stated?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The constitution of Macedonia, which was in force at that time, did not foresee the use of the army at home, particularly the army forces. In order to use the army forces, first it was necessary to proclaim a state of emergency, and then start using the army against the various insurgents in this case the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, now, if we look at the communique, in the first paragraph, I quote: "In order to regularise the armed struggle against the NLA on the Albanian, the Macedonian state also began to prepare legal support by the Macedonia parliament, something that would certainly have taken place de jure, but for the advice of the European institution because the Macedonian state has de facto done this in the military sector without the approval of the parliament." Then, General, you mention that: "The Macedonian state has engaged all the military and police structures it has available in the ongoing combat," and you mention some of these forces. General, why -- what were you trying to say when you were mentioning -- when you were drying this difference between de facto and de jure?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: De facto, it was a state of emergency, because in actual fact they were operating as if de jure there was such a state of emergency, which in fact it was not proclaimed by parliament, de jure.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we move now to this other -- if we could go first in e-court to the first page. I see that we have the second page in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, you go on indicating: "We shall give only some of these forces; for example," and I just mentioned some of them: "The communications regiment, the Skorpions mercenary unit with 900 members, the Wolves special task unit, the Tigers special police unit, the special police emergency unit, the infantry battalion in Skopje, the military police battalion in Shkup, and so on. You keep listing also, I believe, different forces in different locations. Why, General, did you indicate the forces in this communique which were involved?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, as I said, to produce facts that the state of war was in place, even though it was not proclaimed as such; second, I wanted to inform the domestic and international public of the forces participating in this war, based on the information that I had access to at that time; and, thirdly, to -- for others to understand the significance of the ongoing fights.

utterances.speaker: MR. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please go to the second page in e-court in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, just in Albanian version, it will be just two lines below item 4, letter C. You indicated that you wrote: "Given what is cited above, state of emergency has been de facto been brought into being within Macedonia. It has simply not been institutionalised, and it has secretly been directed against the Albanian people, by whose votes President Trajkovski was elected." Then you go on: "Conducting a war policy of this type represents the failure of the policy of agreement." General, what was, again, the importance of stating these facts in the communique?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I already pointed out the importance of these facts; namely, to inform the international community, the internal public, all the citizens of what was going on; to provide data on the use of the army for a war, without the decision of parliament on that; that Mr. Trajkovski had already received the votes of the Albanians when he was elected; and that was his duty to take care of the Albanians and citizens the Macedonia. We wanted to have negotiations and find democratic solutions through dialogue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General. Finally, we read the last three lines of the document, and I quote: "Neither the UCK nor Kosovo nor Albania either are responsible for this, but neither is KFOR, which regularly confirms that UCK forces are not crossing the Kosovo-Macedonia border." What is the significance, General, of this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time of the fighting, there was a propaganda going on through the mass media, that this activity was being carried out through the territory of Albania and Kosovo, based on the presumption that a NLA had developed from the north up to the zone around the border with Kosova and Albania. Everybody who knows that, in the Republic of Macedonia, the Albanians live exclusively on the western part of this Republic, will understand the lack of logic in this statement, because, in this case, they would have turned their backs to the forces of the army and the police. This is what I wanted to make clear at that time, to tell the truth about the facts; that is in this case, KFOR did what it was supposed to, and that Albania and Kosova was not to blame for anything going on. On the contrary, they were stating that we should stop the fighting and sit down at a negotiating table, to resolve the questions of the rights of the Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General. I will seek to tender this communique into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P508, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please go to 65 ter 679, which is tab 20.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, this communique bears the name of Ali Ahmeti, also in the lower part of the document. It starts with: "The UCK NLA is following with close attention the engagement of the international community, to stabilize the situation in Macedonia, and find ways of putting an end to this crisis. We welcome these initiatives which directly contribute to putting an end to the fighting." General, briefly, again was the NLA still supportive at that time of the involvement of the international community in order to stop the conflict?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was in conformity also with our demands, something that we express in every communique we issued.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, in the second paragraph, we read: "The UCK would like to set out its position with regard to the formation of a coalition government." Item 1 reads: "The formation of the coalition government, the primary purpose of which is to isolate the NLA, is of no assistance in resolving the problem and is causing deep concern within the UCK and rendering impossible the establishment of advantageous conditions for a frank and open dialogue." Item 2 -- I will stop there, General. Why did you state -- why, actually, this communique reads that the coalition government would not allow a productive dialogue at that time?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on information we had, the government of the Republic of Macedonia at that time showed two faces, two stands. One stand towards the international community and one stand at -- another stand at home. It was -- one stand was good, which we liked, for a government to be set up and to start negotiations and publish the document from the agreement from the negotiations. But there was the other part as well, which the prime minister elaborated on the 13th of May, when this government was formed, in which one or two duties of this government were the fight on the NLA. This was why we thought that it was difficult to contribute to the solution of this question. What I already said is you can find in the records of the speech by the prime minister on the day when this government was formed.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, again, in item 2, you mention that: "The NLA is willing to reach agreement of a cease-fire." And in item 4, you put forward a proposal in order to reach, what you call, "a genuine democracy." The first item of this proposal is: "An historic agreement must be concluded between the Albanians and the Macedonians, with international mediation. "The Macedonian government, the NLA, and the political parties must participate in this agreement. This agreement must contain undertakes from both parties, so that it will be implemented; and only thus will conditions for the establishment of peace and security in Macedonia be attained." General, why was important to reach this agreement between Albanians Macedonians, but with international mediation?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because from our experience at that time and now, we know that international mediation it is very hard to come to terms between us.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this communique into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P509.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, did the NLA sit and talk to the Albanian political parties during 2001, during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: When was that, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I am not mistake - don't hold me to my word - I think it was in May, the Prizren Agreement, which was reached -- shall I say it? Shall I speak more about this, or are you going to ask me?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, General, I would like to ask you what is the content of this Prizren Agreement, please.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This agreement embodied most of communique number 6, the memorandum, with some minor supplements, among which was the building of a secular state.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: How the Macedonian political parties reacted to this agreement that you reach?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning, they misunderstood it, reacted very badly, both the government and the political parties who proclaimed the political leaders as traitors, those who led the democratic party of Albanian, the PPD. But the aim was to unify the stance of the NLA and the political parties of Albanians in Macedonia, so that together it would be easier for us to resolve these problems, because we saw the dialogue was coming nearer.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And, General, from the NLA side, who participate in these negotiations and in these agreements; and, secondly, from the Albanian political parties, which political parties participated, if you can recall in this agreement, in the Prizren Agreement?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember present was the leader -- the political leader of the NLA; the chairman of the Democratic Party of Albanian, Arben Xhaferi; and the chairman of the Party for Democratic Prosperity, Imer Imeri. Of course, there were people who assisted them, but they weren't the main protagonists of the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, just to have it in the record, when you referred to the political leader of the NLA, you are talking about Ali Ahmeti; correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, my apologies, but before I fail -- when we were talking about the former communique, which became Exhibit P509 - and you still have on your screen - I fail to ask you if you aware of the date, the approximate date, when this communique was issued?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must have been prior to the formation of the government, prior to the coalition government, extended coalition government. It was at the time of efforts made by Mr. Solana and other international representatives to form a coalition government. This communique in the -- at the time of the preliminary talks, when the NLA expressed its opinion.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And which was the approximate date, General, if you can remember a year, approximately?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall it, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And which month? You cannot recall either?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must have been the end of May, but I don't like to put myself in this position, to just to guess. I like to be precise, to speak about what I know. I don't think I can contribute to this trial if I just make suppositions.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General. I appreciate that. You just mentioned Mr. Solana briefly. Who was Mr. Solana? Which position he was he holding at that time?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was responsible for the security issues in Europe.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we move please to 65 ter 682, tab 21.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, this communique is dated 7th of June 2001 and also bears the name of Ali Ahmeti in the lower part of the document. The communique starts reading: "The UCK NLA is following with concern the situation on the ground, where tensions have increased on a daily basis, following the public indication of the Macedonian Academy of Science and Arts proposal for a change to the borders of the Republic of Macedonia and the call by the Prime Minister Ljubco Georgievski for open war against the Albanian population in the Republic of Macedonia." And, indeed, you mention just below some talks held by the government of the Macedonia in order to purchase weapons. General, I'd like to ask you about this proposal of the Macedonian Academy of Science and Arts. What was the proposal in particular?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I try to be brief, because I don't think I with elaborate on it now. The Academy of Sciences, one fine morning, published a text on the division of Macedonia as a proposal by this academy of the Republic of Macedonia, something which implied the change of the population. It had a very negative impact on the already exacerbated situation; therefore, it had to -- he had to give his own opinion, stating that he was not in favour of partitioning the Republic of Macedonia and reestablishment of the borders.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: When you refer to "he," who are you talking about? He had to give his opinion?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The General Staff led by the political representative.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, if we move to the second paragraph, indeed, the General Staff indicated that: "The UCK is in favour of maintaining the integrity and sovereignty of the Republic of Macedonia and condemns any attempts by any institution or group whatsoever which opposes this." Just four lines below, again: "The UCK appeals to all extremists not to redraw borders." And, General, was this the NLA position with regards to this proposal?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The documents issued by the NLA and its General Staff, that was the unwavering stand. Even to this day, I stand by this position.

utterances.speaker: MR. REGUE
utterances.text: I believe that, in page 45, line 16, it has been recorded as "No." So I think the witness mentioned all the documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, again, in the third paragraph, you are -- the NLA is asking for a bilateral cease-fire, and, again, the constructive dialogue is mentioned. Finally, the NLA actually declares a cease-fire of 24 hours, starting on the 7th of June, as long it is not provoked by the military and police forces of the Republic of Macedonia government." General, why did you decide to declare this cease-fire on the 7th of June?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did in order to demonstrate our goodwill to stop the war in real terms.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will seek to tender this communique into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P510 Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could move to 65 ter 683, which is tab 22. Just for the record, the proposal that the communique mentioned issued by the Academy of Science can be found in Exhibit P494, pages 12, 13, 14.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, we have here a communique dated the 11th of June, 2001, where a cease-fire is declared from 11th of June until the 12th of June. General, why was this cease-fire declared at that time?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Always as a sign of goodwill, of wanting peace and negotiations.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Was the cease-fire compiled with by the NLA, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is difficult to remember now such -- something that happened on the 11th of June, 2001. Probably, it must have been compiled with, but I can't precisely remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P511, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please go to 65 ter 685, tab 23.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, this communique, I quote, there mentions: "The NLA is following with particular interest all developments in Macedonia and internationally, related to halting the fightings and especially welcomes in this respect the message of NATO Secretary-General, Mr. George Robinson [sic], and the EU representative for Foreign and Security Policy, Mr. Javier Solana, to calm the situation. "The UCK announces a cease-fire until the 27th of June, 2001 in order to establish conditions for dialogue. The cease-fire will enter into force at 2400 hours on 14th of June 2001." General, why was significant at that time the intervention of George Robinson and Javier Solana?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the situation was deteriorating and that we needed help of NATO Secretary-General, Lord Robertson, and Javier Solana, and I believe they represented all the opinion of others to help us. As we had already stated, we would welcome any initiative taken by the centres of decision making on a global level; I mean, in the EU, NATO, and the United States. We have issued this communique to give more time. That is the first communique that we proclaimed a cease-fire from this period, from the 14th to the 27th of June, and it is signed by Ali Ahmeti, as you see.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, general.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will seek to tender this communique.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P512, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we move to 65 ter 656, tab 24. It should read 686. 65 ter 686 is not uploaded. Okay. We will work with the hard copies Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, are you feeling okay? Are you feeling fine?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I am. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay. General, do you have tab 24 in front of you? General, this communique reads, and it also issued by Ali Ahmeti. It states, and I quote: "In view of the fact that the international public needs to be informed of the political aims of the NLA and the factual situation with regard to the Albanian population in Macedonia, the OMP General Staff hereby appoints its political representative and places him under obligation in Turkey and other countries in Middle East, Mr. Mevlud Aliu." General, which was the purpose of this communique? What was the purpose of this communication?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is only one example; otherwise, the political representative of the NLA, Mr. Ahmeti, has appointed his representative, his political representatives, to almost all the countries of Europe and to the United States. This is a communique whereby he is informing the public that he is appointed Mr. Aliu in Turkey as his political representative. This was a form of open communications for the citizens, wherever they lived and in the countries they operate, to know that that person was legally authorised to speak on behalf of Mr. Ali Ahmeti. At the time, the NLA made up in a way for the lack of powers that were otherwise exercised by the government of Macedonia, in its dealings with foreign embassies and other international communications. That is why build Mr. Ali Ahmeti needed to have people who could speak on his behalf to the foreign public, because many rallies, large-scale meetings, were organised in other countries, and they should be properly informed of what going on in the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I don't intend to lead you. You mention that one of the purpose of this -- of having these representatives was to inform the population. Did they have any other role? Did they play any other function, these NLA representatives abroad?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that they did what they could, which otherwise Mr. Ali Ahmeti would have done if he travelled to these countries. He would have contacted with all the counterparts that would agree to meet him, to explain the aims of war and what our alternative to ending it were.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And to whom these representatives were reporting to, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Ali Ahmeti appointed them and selected them.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And they --

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They reported directly to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will seek it tendered this communique as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P513, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please call 65 ter 687. It is tab 25.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, this communique is produced by Ali Ahmeti and reads: "As meetings between NATO, the EU, and the UCK NLA in Tetovo area continue, agreement for the withdrawal of UCK forces from the village of Aracinovo was concluded at 1400 hours on 24th June 2001. "All this will be done in cooperation with NATO, the EU, and other international institutions, with a presence in the territory of Macedonia. The meetings are due to continue in days to come." General, which was the purpose of this communique?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose of this communique was to inform all the citizens of the Republic of Macedonia, and in particular the Albanians, that withdrawal from Aracina was not done as a result of the politary [as interpreted] pressure, but out of our goodwill to come closer to a peaceful solution and peace in the country because of the agreement concluded by the bodies you mentioned here: NATO, the EU, and others. For us, at that time, it was a very good signal, a signal that made us happy, because the NLA and its General Staff won the status of a body, with which NATO and other European institutions could talk to. For us, it was a great pleasure which made us believe that soon we would sit down and talk about the demands of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, indeed, the communique mentions that meetings, talks, and agreements were reached between NATO, the EU, and the NLA. Who on behalf of the NLA participated in these negotiations?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During this time, Ali Ahmeti was required to go to Sipkovica before this meeting was held, to prepare for the meeting there and to hold this meeting with the NATO representatives there.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Were you in contact with Ali Ahmeti when the talks were being held, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, I was. I maintained contact through telephone, not direct contact.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And which of the parties who participated in the negotiations, General, initiated the contacts? Who approached who in order to engage in this dialogue?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, so it's my impression then and now, that this issue was raised by the now late president of the Republic of Macedonia, Mr. Trajkovski. He raised this issue with NATO representatives; and later on, I learned that on the 14th of June, I think, he sent a letter to NATO to intervene and contribute to finding a solution to the issue in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, after this contact with the international representatives, how was the relation between the NLA and the international representatives, after this Aracinovo agreement was reached?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't quite hear your question. Could you please repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Sure. After the Aracinovo agreement, how was the relation between the international representatives and the NLA.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, after the withdrawal from Aracin, after this task was completed, the meetings between Ali Ahmeti and NATO representatives continued, and everything was moving into the direction of initiating negotiations that would facilitate an agreement and solution to the crisis in the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will seek to tendered this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P514, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will call 65 ter 778.11, tab 7. It's three maps. If in e-court we could display the page 3, and we have larger copies for Your Honours and for my colleagues and the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, we will look individually at each of these maps, but just to start, I would like to ask you some general questions. Did you produce these maps, General, or these plans?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: When did you produce them?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember producing them on the 5th of July. In fact, they were in my computer stored much earlier, but I worked concretely on this map and produced it on the 5th of July, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And which was the purpose of these maps? Why did you compile them? Why did you produce them?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As Mr. Ali Ahmeti reached an agreement with Peter Feith and others that he talked to, an agreement for a cease-fire, that would make room for a dialogue, I then started to talk to certain NATO generals that were in the company of Mr. Feith. They asked me - of course, with the permission of Ali Ahmeti - to provide them with the areas where our brigades had established their authority. The aim of this map was for the EU and NATO monitoring was familiar with the positions of the NLA, and in case they are violated to undertake the necessary measures to re-establish cease-fire. On this occasion, I provided Mr. Peter Feith with all our positions, after discussing this issue with a NATO general who was in the company of Mr. Peter Feith, but, I'm sorry, I don't remember his name.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, was Peter Feith also member of the NATO?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which person you refer to? Sorry, I didn't hear your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Who was Peter Feith, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe he was the consular to the NATO Secretary-General, Lord Robertson. But what were his concrete duties, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, you mentioned agreement between NATO and Ali Ahmeti about a cease-fire. Can you remember when was there agreement, this cease-fire? When was the agreement reached? When was the cease-fire declared?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, the agreement was signed on the 5th of July, while it entered into force, so in the early hours of the 6th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. REGUE
utterances.text: In page 62, line 10, I believe it should read 5th of July, instead of 35.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, if we can look to the first -- to actually the page which bears ERN R062-6972.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: It is the third page in e-court. The map he has in front of him. The one which bears the ERN R062-6972. The one which has the heading, "Region of the Brigade of the 113."

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, which is the area which we can see in this map?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose of these maps was not to declare these units, but, rather, the territory that was controlled by NLA units; whereas, the declaration of units followed after the agreement for the handover of weapons during the Essential Harvest operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, but if you are aware, which area of Macedonia can we see in this map in front of you, which geographic area?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the first one that we're discussing, 1, we have the area of 113 Brigade; and, during this time, the 114th Brigade was formed out of this brigade. It included the area of Mali i Zi i Shkupit, including the villages of Lojane, Vaksince, Slupcane, Orizar [phoen], Nikustak, Matejce, Nikustak, down below up to Mojance. These were villages situated up to the border with Kosova. What is significant here is the fact that through the engagement of the NLA and the ARM in this territory, there existed a battery, a combined battery, with cannons and tanks of the ARM in the area from Alashece [phoen], in north. It is marked with red on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: It's the red dot that we can see near the border with Serbia. Correct, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These are the border posts, while this dot is on the north of the flag that marks the 113 Brigade of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: For the record, the dot that the witness is referring is the one just above the flag.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, the area that we can see indicated in this map, which is actually depicted by an intermittent black line boarding Serbia, and then it goes with a blue line from the north-east to the south-west, I believe that you already mentioned it, but, General, which brigade of the NLA was operating in that area? Just to have it in the record and very briefly.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this area, marked in this document ending with the figures 972, is the 113 Brigade of the NLA and the newly formed 114th Brigade of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: In the centre of this area, more towards the east, we see a flag with Brigade 113. What were you indicating, General, with this flag?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This flag, based on the regulation on compiling and maintaining maps, it indicates the command of the Brigade 113.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And in which location, in which municipality was this command posted?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During this time, it was in the Otlja village.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could move to the next document. In e-court, it will be page 1; and the ERN, it will end with 6970.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think, before we move to the next document, Ms. Regue, it might be appropriate to have the next break.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And we resume at five past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, if re look at this second map, we can see that the village, the municipality of Tetovo, is depicted in the centre of the map. Then we see an area which is indicated by an intermittent black line bordering Kosovo, and then a blue line which goes from the north-east towards the south-west. General, what does this area show?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The northern border with blue colour is the left border of the brigade of the area of responsibility; while the border with interrupted blue line at Bogovina village is the right border of the brigade; while the border on the background is the border with Kosova, and it's marked with a line that shows a state border. This is the area where 112 Brigade had established its authority.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: NATO did not ask us to show the units under the brigade because it was already cease-fire; while once the peacetime was established, then the other records were to be supplied.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, we see in this area, in the centre, we see, again, a flag which goes out from village of Sipkovica, and we read, "Brigade 112." What were you indicating with this flag, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This flag, according to military rules, depicts the command post, to the area where the brigade command is established, the command of 112 Brigade. It is in the village of Sipkovica.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks General. Now if we look outside this area, we see three circles on the upper right side of the map, three circles also depicted in blue. General, what were you indicating with these three circles, these territories?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These three circles, as I wanted to be more precise at that time, depict the territory that is under 115 Brigade. It had a battalion, and it had some parts in the village of Oraste [phoen] and Neraste [phoen], so that the monitors were familiar with the territory that was under the authority of 115th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: With regards to the circle, which is more towards the right, towards the east of the map, we, again, see a flag which goes out from, I believe, Radusa and reads, "Brigade 115." What were you indicating with this flag, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to rules, it is stated the 1st Battalion of the 115th Brigade. It's number 1/115th Brigade, which means 1st Battalion of 115 Brigade, which is situated in Radush.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Where were the headquarters of the 115th Brigade. If you don't see it in the map General, just mention the municipality, the location.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this particular moment, the 1st Battalion and the headquarters of this brigade are together in Radush; but since the forces do not amount to a brigade force, it is it marked at a level of a battalion. So there is the command of the battalion and the headquarters of the battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could move to page in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And now, General, we are going to look at the map, which bears the ERN 6971. General, in this map, we see towards the west, almost near the border with Albania, a circle with an intermittent blue line. What were you indicating, General, with this circle?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area, where the 1st Battalion of 116th Brigade is positioned, is a mountainous region, and it is very difficult to encircle the territory under this brigade with just one line. The interrupted line, according to the rules, depicts the possible area that is controlled by the brigade, while the full line is a precise area controlled by the brigade. So, as I said, it wasn't possible to be more determined, due to the relief of the territory. So that's why I depicted it in this form, and it was accepted as such by NATO authorities.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And, General, we see inside this intermittent -- within this circle marked with intermittent line, another circle with a full line. What were you indicating? Just briefly, General, what were you indicating with regards to this circle?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The interrupted line depicts the potential or possible area, while the full line, the actual area, where the brigade, the NLA has authority.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And we see, again, General, a flag with the numbers and letters, "1/Brigade 116." What were you indicating, General, with this flag?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This flag shows that here the 1st Battalion of the 116th Brigade is functioning.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And where were the headquarters of this 1st Battalion of the 116th Brigade, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The brigade and battalion headquarters were together at a location called Kuku Zabel [phoen]. This can be seen only if you use the map to see the command post.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is in the area of Tanusevci village and other villages in municipality of Gostivar.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will seek to tender these three maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The maps will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As exhibit P515, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise for interrupting my colleague. But before the maps are received, on the third map, the witness stated exactly which area was under the control of the 116th Brigade. As far as I was able to follow the trial, regarding the first map shown to us, the area around Kumanovo, as well as regarding the area around Tetovo, the witness did not state whether the marked area was under the NLA control. Did the entire area that was marked, was it under the NLA control, so for -- to make it more precise for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I understood, Mr. Apostolski, that the third map was different because of the terrain in that area. Because of that, there was difficulty being precise as to the area. So two circles were drawn: One, if I can paraphrase it, about which the witness was absolutely certain, and then the dotted intermittent line about which that may have been the case. So I think it is only the third nap is affected in way.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: That was my understanding, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If you have lingering doubts, they can be followed up in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could go to 65 ter 778.18, which is tab 12.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, we have in front of us a present statement made by NATO spokesman, Major Barry Johnson, at a press briefing on the 6th of August 2001. This document has the heading, the title, "NATO background on the plan Essential Harvest, 6 August 2001. The operation will be conducted in three phases." In the first paragraph of this document, Mr. Johnson mentions that: "Although the details of the plan remain to be discussed by NATO and the Ministry of Defence, the concept has been fully developed and troops from contributing nations are prepared to begin deployment within 48 hours. "Within two weeks of receiving an order to deploy, Taskforce Harvest would be fully operational and ready to conduct its 30 day mission for collecting weapons and ammunition." If we move to the third paragraph, it reads: "The plan called operation Essential Harvest could result in the deployment of about 3500 soldiers from various NATO members nations." General, are you familiar with the operation or plan Essential Harvest?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am, on a political level. It was all the NLA political representative, Ali Ahmeti, that discussed these issues; whereas, the issues concerning the collection of weapons, it was me who dealt with this issue, together with NATO officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, you partially answered my next question, but what was the significance of the plan, of the operation Essential Harvest? What was the importance?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is of great importance because this was conditioned. We were supposed to hand over the weapons, while the parliament was supposed to get ready to carry out the changes based on the Ohrid Agreement. So we were getting ready to carry out this task and fulfil our part of the obligation.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General. If we read below, in the English version, it will be the fifth paragraph in the first page. It reads: "Before the troops can be deployed, certain conditions must, of course, be met. These include an unconditional cease-fire, the signing of a framework document and its annexes by the government's political parties, and a technical agreement with the so-called UCK to voluntarily hand over their weapons." General, with regards to this technical agreement with the NLA, was this agreement -- was this agreement reached to hand over the weapons?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was reached, and it was signed by the NLA political representative, who was at the same time the commander of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And which other parties signed this agreement, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: NATO. The NLA signed this agreement only with NATO.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General. Which role did you play in the implementation of this agreement?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to point out that I was committed to planning and implementing this agreement on the voluntary surrender of weapons that were at the disposal of the National Liberation Army, in conformity with the plan and the dates of the agreement between the NLA and NATO. I made all necessary preparations. I maintained continuous contact with NATO officers and monitors who were engaged, involved in the collection of weapons. The areas or locations were designated where which brigade will hand over the weapons and on which date. Before that, there was an assessment made, together with Mr. Ali Ahmeti and NATO representatives, as to the amount of weapons that the NLA was to hand over. May I continue? The NATO, at that time, estimated that the National Liberation Army had to hand over 3.333 weapons. We agreed with this figure, and we started the collection of weapons at positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General. Can I interrupt you there briefly. General, when you were performing your duties in the implementation of this agreement, were you working together with NATO representatives?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: By all means, because the handover of weapons was carried out by the NLA, by every soldier in person, while the reception the collection, the transportation of these weapons was carried out by NATO and its troops. At the same time, the security of the location, where this was taking place, was provided by the forces of the Essential Harvest operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General. In the next page in the English version, I think that we are still in the Albanian page, General, page 2 in e-court of the English version, we can see how Major Barry Johnson explains three phases with regards to this operation. Are you familiar with these phases, General, or you want me to read them to you?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you wish. I am aware of them, because I was the one who did the work. But if you feel like it, you may.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay, General. I'll just ask whether the plan was implemented following the stages, the phases that we see in this document, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The plan was implemented as foreseen. It was very difficult for us to implement it because when it was approved, before that happened, we wanted the NLA members to be placed in several barracks. And after the surrender of the weapons finished - I apologise - after 30 days, the members of the NLA should be obliged to wait in their positions for 30 days in order to surrender the weapons. Initially, I was afraid they might go home with the weapons, and it would be very hard for us to collect them; but, apparently, they showed a very high level of moral and a very high sense of responsibility, because the handing over of the weapons was a condition for the political changes to take place later. So, when it happened according to plan that we had drawn in cooperation with Harvest, there were 500 more weapons than the initial number of 3.383 [as interpreted]. So there were 3875 weapons all together, because everyday new volunteers came to the brigades, and they couldn't turn them back, but all the weapon, as I said, were surrendered.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P516, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Can we go, please, to 65 ter 778.17, which is in tab 11.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, we have in front of us another document, which bears the title, "The National Liberation Army," and then we see in the upper left side the date, 4th August 2001, for the attention of the NLA brigades. The subject of this document is: "Order from the Chief of the General Staff. Indeed, we see, at least we see in the second page of the English and in the original, your signature, General. General, did you produce this document?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Just briefly, General, which was the purpose of this document?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander was preparing the demobilisation of the NLA, and his idea was for it to take part in all its segments. Based on this idea, I instructed that the brigades prepare for surrendering their weapons, and the administration to see to regulating this issue with all the members. That is the purpose of this instruction.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General. Indeed, we can read in the different items of this document. Item 1: "A proof of membership of soldiers and officers of the NLA is to be established for all brigades and other units of the General Staff." Then item 2 mentions the creation of a commission at the brigade level, which this commission needs to work together and following the plan drafted with the approval of the brigade command. Then in item 4: "The commission will carry out the following activities," and you, General, mentioned, indicated, and I quote: "It will fill out military discharge forms with all the dates, details. It will photograph all members and place the first and last name of the individual in question on the photo, as well as the number from the military discharge form, and the photographs with the names and numbers of the individuals are to be stored electronically." General, what was the significance of these preparatory activities?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the NLA, just like in any other army, there are people who have joined it, who have participated in fighting. First, it is necessary to have accurate data on them; then to set up a commission which I mentioned here, composed of several members, among whom there should be doctors, possibly psychologists, teaches, and lawyers, so that they will take note of the participants in the brigades of the NLA, and verify whether the person who has joined has been injured in the course of the war; then records should be taken of the time he joined, with whom he joined in the NLA, and in what status he has been discharged. If he is in a healthy condition, then that should be noted. So this had to be done upon the signing of the Ohrid Agreement, and then work should start by this commission.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Indeed, General, in item 5, we read: "Activities pursuant to this order are to begin on the date of the signing of the political agreement and will end within two weeks." With this politina [sic] agreement that you are mentioning, General, are you referring to the Ohrid Framework Political Agreement?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But on that date, I didn't know that it would be called the Ohrid Framework Agreement. For me, it would be a political agreement, then that is the name that they referred to it as, the Ohrid Framework Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what it refers to.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Simply, we don't object to the admission of the document, to make that point clear. However, we understand that Mr. Ostreni has been careful to describe the document as an instruction. In fact, during proofing, he made it clear to the Prosecution that the translation of that document, from the Albanian to the English as an "order," was inaccurate; and that, in effect, it should read as a "recommendation." I believe that is the sense that the witness wished to give to that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can clarify this matter. Maybe it is my fault.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, in English, we read "order." Was this document an order, or it has another term?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have the right to give orders. I could only give instructions or make recommendations. If the commander ordered me that I should issue an order on his behalf, then I should do that. In this case, it is simply an instruction or a recommendation.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I thank Mr. Mettraux for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The document will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P517, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, are you aware who were the signatory parties of the Ohrid Agreement? Who signed the Ohrid Agreement basically, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are many people. The head of the state; I think also the prime minister, if I'm not mistaken, because it happened six years ago; there are the political party representatives; and then the representatives of the European Union; the representative of the United States.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Was the NLA a signatory party of the Ohrid Agreement, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Directly, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Had the NLA any sort of contact with the parties who signed the Ohrid Agreement during the negotiations, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The political representative of the NLA was in regular contacts with the leaders who signed the Prizren Agreement. The Democratic Party of Albanian, the Party for Democratic Prosperity, sometimes with the party led by Kastriot Haxhirexha - I don't remember the party; it was kind of national party - so he was in contact.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And if you have the knowledge, General, which was the content of these discussions, of these contacts?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The content of these discussions was what was already discussed, finding a solution which actually led to the Ohrid Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did the NLA support the Ohrid Agreement, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did, and it still does; as a former member, I'm talking.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did the Ohrid Agreement reproduce the NLA demands, General?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, yes, almost all of them. But when we talk of an agreement, if both parties are not satisfied 100 percent, then it's okay. But if only one side is very content, then it is not a good agreement. I think we supported, and I think it is a good agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Can we please call 65 ter 440, 4-4-0. It's in tab 28. Before that, Your Honours, I didn't try to mislead with the Chamber with omission that, indeed, the witness was correct in proofing. I was more concerned about speeding up the proceedings, so I apologise if I made that omission.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We didn't think that our colleague was trying to mislead you in any way. We simply indicate, I think, that because of our interruption, the document has not yet been admitted, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I thought it was Exhibit 517.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In that case, I must have missed a few lines of the transcript. I am grateful.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, I think, you are right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please continue, Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: General, do you have in front of you a document from the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Republic of Macedonia? You can read in the upper left side that this document is submitted by Major Gjorgji Mitrev, and the date is the 22nd ever September, 2001, Skopje. It is submitted to the headquarters of Operative Action, Ramno, DOD, the Ministry of Internal Affairs, sector for security and police station for the security of government facilities and diplomatic consular representations. This document is an Official Note, which bears the title, "Possible violations of the public peace on a larger scale at the police academy, Idrizevo." The first two lines read: "The course for 110 candidates for police trainees of Albanian ethnicity has been announced to start on the 24th of September, 2001 at the police academy in Idrizevo." General, are you familiar about the training that was foreseen within the police academy for new recruits of Albanian ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware of the tendency to improve as fast as possible the ethnic composition of the police force in the Republic of Macedonia. That started right after the signing of the Ohrid Framework Agreement, and I do know that efforts were made in this regard, in order to form police -- mixed police patrols with Albanians, Macedonians, Turks, and other minorities, but mainly Albanians, in order to build trust and confidence of the population in the police force.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: This document talks about a meeting which was held the 22nd of September of 2001 at this police academy, and it lists -- it indicates the members of this meeting. And if we read just below the names of the participants: "A single issue was discussed, which is the arrival of the mentioned number of police trainee candidates from security aspect regarding the facility they shall be placed and train." If we go to the second page, I believe that in both languages the documents -- the document indicates that: "At the moment, several units of the Ministry of Internal Affairs are positioned as follows: A battalion for rapid intervention," illegible, "Tigers, and the police reserve force unit, whose number amounts to 800 to 1.000 members. "During the discussion, it is has been pointed out to all participants of the meeting, that there are open threats by members of the aforementioned units, that they will prevent with all means the entering of the mentioned number of candidates, including also the use of fire-arms or explosive materials." General, were you aware with the problems encounter by these new Albanian police recruits in late 2001.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may only say that I heard that there were problems.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And the document goes on indicating that: "The above mentioned information point to the chance of violation of public peace and order on a larger scale of a heavier incidents, in case the start of the announced course is realised in the mentioned facility." General, which problems did you hear, that these new recruits were having?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard what you already read to me, that the police forces reacted adversely to that, and that after a time we heard that there were problems with Mr. Pardew who went there for a visit after, I think -- because the United States, I think, funded the training, and he went there to check on the -- to see how money was being spent. And it was a critical report published in the media against Mr. Pardew that he been very severe in his stand, but I can't make a comment on that. But I only know that there were problems.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, General.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will seek to tendered this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, in view of Your Honours ruling, I won't attempt to have it unadmitted. I will simply indicate that if the content of the document had, in fact, been relevant to the Prosecution case, it could and should, in our submissions, have been put through a witness capable of giving information in relation to the content. The witness, Mr. Ostreni, has given information to the extent he was capable about information which he had in his possession. We'll simply indicate that Mr. Galevski, for one, later became the director of the police academy in question. If there had been any question about this particular incident, in our submissions, it should have been put to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will become Exhibit P518, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We must now adjourn for the day.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And I have no further questions, Your Honours, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well I'll let you contemplate that overnight in case, but we resume tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 9th day of November, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.49 p.m.,
